results.title: Seoul's spy agency issues cybersecurity advisory for flaws found in programming language Java
results.content: The National Intelligence Service (NIS) has sent a security advisory to public institutions regarding a vulnerability found in the widely used computer language Java, industry sources said Tuesday. The vulnerability could allow malicious actors to carry out remote code execution of Java-based apps without authentication, which could lead to major service disruptions and data leakages, the advisory said, according to the sources. Java is a widely used programming language currently being maintained by Oracle Corp. and is widely used to build Android apps, back-end server systems at banks and cloud computing services. The NIS rated the vulnerability as "critical," the highest among four tiers in the common vulnerability scoring system (CVSS), a standardized framework to measure the technical severity of software and system security vulnerabilities. results.title: Lee calls for thorough crackdown against AI-assisted cheating during CSAT
results.content: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called on officials Tuesday to thoroughly prepare anti-cheating measures for the nationwide college entrance exam set to take place this week, describing cheating as a "grave crime" that undermines social trust. Lee made the remarks during an emergency meeting to inspect the country's readiness for the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), also known in Korean as Suneung, scheduled for Thursday, following widespread concerns over cheating using artificial intelligence (AI). "The Suneung is a symbol of fairness and a ladder of opportunity in our society," Lee said during a video meeting held from Manila, as he wrapped up his visit to the city for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. results.title: Student files constitutional petition against gov't decision to conduct CSAT as scheduled
results.content: A high school student on Tuesday filed a constitutional complaint against the government's decision to proceed with the nationwide college entrance exam as scheduled, amid ongoing fears over cheating using artificial intelligence (AI). The move comes as Korea has been rocked by the recent confession by the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam that he cheated with the help of AI and digital devices. The incident deepened worries that such a method could be used in Thursday's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), prompting the government to announce a series of measures to prevent the exam from being undermined by AI-assisted cheating. Among the anti-cheating measures announced were physical checking of all glasses worn by test takers, covering buttons on their clothes with stickers and a blockage of Wi-Fi networks inside and near the test sites. results.title: Veteran catcher remains with Bears as KBO free agency opens
results.content: Veteran catcher Yang Eui-ji re-signed with the Doosan Bears on Tuesday as free agency opened in Korean baseball. Yang became the first of 22 free agents to land a contract this offseason in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO), as he signed a two-year deal worth up to 5.5 billion won ($4.1 million). He will earn 1 billion won in total annual salary and 4 billion won in signing bonus. He can make another 500 million won in incentives. Yang, 39, first played for the Bears from 2007 to 2018. He then joined the NC Dinos as a free agent and played there from 2019 to 2022. He reunited with the Bears prior to the 2023 season. In the four seasons during his second tour of duty, Yang has batted .301 with 77 home runs and 330 RBIs — leading the club in all three categories during that span. results.content: MANILA — U.S. President Donald Trump said Tuesday that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un "would like to" attend this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China, leaving open the possibility of a meeting between the two leaders. "He would like to, yeah. We'll see what happens," Trump said during a meeting with leaders of the Quad security grouping on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila, when asked whether Kim would attend the APEC summit. The remarks came after Trump raised the possibility of meeting Kim during his visit to Shenzhen, China, for the APEC summit, scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday. On Monday, before departing for his Asia trip, Trump told reporters at the White House that he "may meet with" Kim. "He may come; I don't know. results.title: Tennis star Chung Hyeon vows to put up good fight in Davis Cup quarters
results.content: With Korea headed to its first appearance in the quarterfinals of the top international men's tennis team competition next week, one of the country's top stars said Tuesday he will try to fight the good fight against a heavily favored opponent. Korea will make its debut at the Davis Cup Final 8 next week at BolognaFiere in Bologna, Italy. The Davis Cup is the premier international team event in men's tennis and Korea will take on the three-time defending champion Italy in the quarterfinals at 4 p.m. next Wednesday (local time), or 12:00 a.m. Thursday. Chung Hyeon, the semifinalist at the 2018 Australian Open, said he will look to recapture the glory from eight years ago. results.title: Universities can bridge competing interests to turn research into impact
results.content: Universities can bring competing businesses, policymakers and scholars to the same table, experts said at the Times Higher Education (THE) Innovation & Impact Summit 2026, arguing that their value lies as much in connecting various areas of expertise as in producing them. Speaking during Tuesday’s session, titled, “Higher education, industry and government: Achieving effective collaboration,” at Korea University in Seoul, panelists said successful partnerships require more than funding research and waiting for businesses for commercialization. John Kao, president of National Tsing Hua University, pointed to Taiwan’s semiconductor industry as an example of cooperation built over decades, with universities nurturing students, government supporting industrial transformation and companies building relationships across global supply chains. results.title: Ideas become impact when universities, startups, big businesses team up: Finda CEO
results.content: Universities play a significant role in turning ideas into real-world impact by developing the knowledge and workforce that businesses need, Finda co-founder and CEO Lee Hye-min said during the Times Higher Education (THE) Innovation & Impact Summit 2026 at Korea University in Seoul. Speaking Tuesday in a student success story session, Lee said innovation depended on cooperation between institutions with different strengths, rather than entrepreneurs acting alone. “Universities create new knowledge and train the next generation of talent,” she said. Startups take ideas into the market and test them, while established businesses contribute scale, customers, data and capital. “When these three work together, ideas turn into real impact,” Lee said. results.title: Lee, Takaichi address upcoming US-China-Russia talks
results.content: MANILA — President Lee Jae Myung and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stressed the importance of strategic communication as major powers are stepping up discussions on peace and stability in Northeast Asia, Cheong Wa Dae said Tuesday. They discussed the regional issues during their bilateral talks in Manila, held on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit and related gatherings in the Philippines. Their bilateral talks drew attention for their implications for South Korea-Japan ties as well as regional security ahead of a three-way summit among the leaders of the United States, China and Russia slated for Thursday. results.title: AMPERS&ONE aims to forge inner strength with 1st full-length album
results.content: K-pop boy band AMPERS&ONE returned Tuesday with its first full-length album, "PATHFINDER," declaring its determination to forge its own way three years after its debut. The seven-piece multinational group, consisting of Kamden, Brian, Jiho, Siyun, Kyrell, Mackiah and Seungmo, debuted in November 2023 under FNC Entertainment, home to acts including FTISLAND, SF9 and P1Harmony. Since then, the group has steadily expanded its presence at home and abroad, most recently completing its "Born To Define" tour, which began in Seoul in May and took the members to 27 cities across the United States, Asia and Europe. Building on the momentum, AMPERS&ONE is now looking to mark a new chapter with "PATHFINDER" and its lead single, "King's Way." results.title: Court grants LIG D&A's request to suspend 2-yr bidding ban
results.content: LIG Defense & Aerospace (LIG D&A) said Tuesday a court had granted its request to suspend a two-year ban on its participation in defense procurement bids imposed by Korea's arms procurement agency. LIG D&A sought a suspension of the ban from the Seoul Administrative Court after the Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) imposed the sanction last month following the indictment of company executives on charges of bribing a DAPA official in connection with weapons procurement tenders. In a regulatory filing, LIG D&A said the court suspended the ban pending a first-instance ruling in its lawsuit challenging the sanction. If the company wins, it can continue bidding for defense contracts. If it loses, the two-year ban will take effect 30 days after the ruling. results.title: Temporary head coach for nat'l football team to return to native Spain after final match
results.content: Robert Moreno, caretaker manager for the men's national football team, will not travel back to Korea after coaching his likely final match against Qatar on Tuesday, the sport's national federation said. The Korea Football Association (KFA) said Moreno and his staff will return to their native Spain instead, following Korea's friendly match in Doha, set to kick off at 5 p.m. (local time), or 11 p.m. (Korea time) Tuesday. The KFA hired Moreno in early September on a temporary basis, putting him in charge of six matches from September to November. The Spanish tactician stepped in for Hong Myung-bo, who had resigned in late June following Korea's elimination from the group stage at the FIFA World Cup. results.title: S. Koreans split on directly raising N. Korean human rights: survey
results.content: South Koreans are split over whether Seoul should take issue with North Korean human rights violations, a survey showed Tuesday. The poll, jointly conducted by the Seoul-based Database Center for North Korean Human Rights and Consumer Insight on 1,000 adults from Sept. 9-17, found 52 percent opposed Seoul's raising the issue directly. Asked about the likely effect of raising the issue directly, 74.3 percent said it would hurt inter-Korean relations, 15.2 percent expected no effect and 10.5 percent expected a positive one. Interest in North Korean human rights remained relatively high at 63.1 percent. Among the reasons cited, feeling empathy for North Koreans ranked first at 26.6 percent, followed by the shared history of the two Koreas as one nation at 17 percent. results.title: Korea joins NATO-led Starlift space initiative to boost launch capabilities
results.content: Korea has joined a space initiative led by the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) in an effort to secure rapid and reliable satellite launch capabilities, the defense ministry said Tuesday. The ministry signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with NATO on the Starlift program in Brussels on Oct. 29, becoming the first non-NATO member country to join the initiative, according to the ministry. Joining the program will bolster Korea's reliable access to space by diversifying the military's launch options and expand opportunities for the domestic space industry in overseas markets, it said in a release. "In particular, gaining access to participating nations' launch vehicles and space ports will allow Korea to reduce its dependence on specific foreign launch providers," it added. results.title: Jung Ho-yeon named among potential Bond girls, raising prospect of Korean first
results.content: Korean actress Jung Ho-yeon, who rose to global fame through Netflix's "Squid Game," has been named among 45 actresses suggested by U.S. fashion magazine Vogue as potential Bond girls for the next James Bond film, raising the possibility that she could become the first Korean actress to take on the role. The speculation comes as Hollywood actor Robert Pattinson has been named the next James Bond, drawing attention to who might star opposite him in the upcoming installment of the long-running spy franchise. On Sunday, Vogue published a list of 45 actresses it considered suitable for the next Bond film, placing Jung fifth on the list. The magazine highlighted Jung's breakout performance in "Squid Game" and her appearance in director Na Hong-jin's film "Hope." results.title: UC Berkeley offers blueprint for university-driven startup hubs
results.content: Connecting scattered campus programs and overhauling top-down incentives turned the University of California (UC), Berkeley, into the world’s leading producer of startup founders, a university official said Tuesday, offering a blueprint for other institutions. “Turns out it’s not rocket science,” Darren Cooke, the university’s chief innovation and entrepreneurship officer, said in a keynote speech at the Times Higher Education (THE) Innovation & Impact Summit 2026 in Seoul. UC Berkeley, a public university in California’s San Francisco Bay area, edged out nearby Stanford University four years ago in PitchBook’s annual ranking of universities whose alumni found venture-backed startups and has widened its lead since, Cooke said. results.title: Chagall returns to Seoul with exhibition tracing art shaped by turmoil
results.content: One of Marc Chagall’s famous works depicting lovers floating above rooftops and animals defying gravity has long captivated Korean audiences. That work, "Bride and Groom with Eiffel Tower" is in Seoul for a new exhibition, “Chagall, Ever Crossing,” which is scheduled to open on Nov. 24 at Centre Pompidou Hanwha in Seoul. As one of the most beloved non-Korean artists in the country, this isn't Chagall's first exhibition in Korea. However, this latest exhibition is expected to be different as visitors will be invited to look beyond the familiar image of the painter of love and fantasy — and consider the turbulent history beneath his luminous colors. The exhibition brings together 65 original works, including 57 paintings and eight sculptures and ceramics from the French institution’s collection. results.title: Korean, Japanese stars team up for cross-border manhunt in Netflix's 'The Blue Road'
results.content: Korean star Son Suk-ku and acclaimed Japanese actor Eita Nagayama join forces for a high-stakes cross-border manhunt in Netflix’s upcoming thriller "The Blue Road." Adapted from the hit Korean-Japanese webtoon, the series follows the two detectives as they hunt down a brutal serial killer leaving behind a trail of grotesque corpses and cryptic messages across international borders. The series is directed by Han Jun-hee, whose credits include the films "Coin Locker Girl" (2015) and "Hit-and-Run Squad" (2019), as well as Netflix’s hit series "D.P." Seasons 1 (2021) and 2 (2023). Han recalled his encounter with the original work about two decades ago. results.title: PM announces package of measures to prevent cheating on college entrance exam
results.content: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook announced a series of measures Tuesday to shield this week's nationwide college entrance exam from cheating using artificial intelligence, including banning all smart devices from test rooms, deploying thousands of additional personnel and covering all buttons of test takers' clothing with stickers. In a special address to the nation, Han also vowed to deal sternly with any cheaters, including banning them from the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) for 10 years, punishing them criminally and canceling college admissions in case their cheating is uncovered after admission. "Under the firm principle that the honest efforts of students must not be undermined by cheating, the government will concentrate all capabilities on this issue from proactive prevention and test site supervision to post-exam investigations and punishment," Han said. results.title: Police book 86 people over illegal drug network
results.content: Police said Tuesday they have booked 86 people on suspicions of selling and purchasing illegal drugs through a network mostly formed by personal ties. Of the 86, 45 individuals are suspected of selling or giving away drugs, such as methamphetamine, marijuana and LSD, through romantic partners, friends, colleagues and fellow prison inmates between July 2024 and September 2026, according to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. The remaining 41 individuals are suspected of purchasing or receiving the drugs for free from the 45 and using them. Police said they have placed 29 of the 86 under arrest and referred them to the prosecution. results.title: Korea set to achieve $1 tril. export milestone for 1st time
results.content: Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan on Tuesday thanked workers in the local port management and logistics sectors for contributing to Korea's achievement of $1 trillion in annual exports. Kim visited a port in the western coastal city of Incheon, the country's major maritime gateway, as the country is nearing the $1 trillion export milestone for 2026. Thanks to strong outbound shipments of semiconductors amid an artificial intelligence (AI) supercycle, the country's cumulative exports exceeded $960 billion as of Nov. 10 and are expected to surpass the $1 trillion mark as early as Thursday or Friday for the first time ever. Korea is expected to become the fourth country in the world to achieve the milestone, following the United States, China and Germany. It took 21 years for Asia's fourth-largest economy to reach $1 trillion in annual exports after first hitting the $100 billion mark in 1995

results.title: 'Impact begins where paper ends,' Korean university execs say
results.content: Korean universities need to judge their success by how research is used in industry and society, not by how often it is cited, the leaders of two Korean universities said Tuesday. Yang O-bong, president of Jeonbuk National University, and Park Jhung-soo, executive vice president for research and external affairs at Ewha Womans University, spoke on a panel at the Times Higher Education Innovation & Impact Summit 2026 in Seoul. The three-day gathering, which runs through Thursday, focuses on turning academic research into commercial and social value. “For me, the impact begins where the paper ends,” Park said. He said Korean academia largely credits achievement through citation indicators such as field-weighted citation impact, which compares a paper’s citations with the world average in its field. results.title: Seoul hosts World Congress of Accountants for 1st time in 122-year history
results.content: The World Congress of Accountants (WCOA), the largest global gathering for the accountancy profession, kicked off in Seoul, Tuesday. It is the first time Korea is hosting the event in WCOA's 122-year history. Co-hosted by the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) and the Korea Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA), the three-day conference brought together around 1,200 accounting professionals, corporate executives and regulators from 120 countries under the theme “Together for a Connected Tomorrow.” “This is a historic moment for Korea,” KICPA President Choi Woon-youl said in his welcoming remarks. “The role of accountants has never been more important. results.title: A Twosome Place launches new edition to Schosaeng Christmas cake
results.content: Premium dessert cafe chain A Twosome Place launched a new addition to its flagship Strawberry Chocolate Cream Cake lineup Tuesday, seeking to strengthen its presence in the country's cake market as the Christmas season approaches. The cake is widely known in Korea as Schosaeng. The new product, Cream Top Schosaeng, features dark chocolate sponge layered with Valrhona crispy pearls, dark chocolate ganache cream and a vanilla bean mascarpone topping. It is the fifth addition to A Twosome Place's Schosaeng Universe, which has previously featured cakes incorporating matcha and Dubai chocolate. First launched in 2014, Schosaeng has earned a strong following among dessert lovers in Korea as one of the country's most popular cake brands. results.title: THE summit calls on universities to bring research discoveries to market
results.content: Universities must turn research breakthroughs into real-world innovation and economic growth, global higher education leaders urged Tuesday as the Times Higher Education (THE) Innovation & Impact Summit 2026 kicked off in Seoul. The three-day summit at Korea University brings together more than 300 leaders and experts from over 150 institutions worldwide to explore how universities can drive innovation and economic growth through research and industry collaboration. Opening the summit, Mei Mei Lim, THE president for the Asia-Pacific region, highlighted Korea’s strong research capabilities, noting that the country invests more than 5 percent of its gross domestic product in research and development, making it one of the world's most research-intensive economies. results.content: U.S. President Donald Trump floated the prospect of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong-un during his trip to China this week, but experts said talks are unlikely in the near term and warned that any eventual deal with Pyongyang could leave South Korea facing new security risks. results.title: 'How could we possibly detect them?' Teachers fear AI cheating; students urge tougher checks
results.content: Fears of students cheating by using artificial intelligence (AI) technology are rattling classrooms before Thursday’s college entrance exam, leaving teachers increasingly unsure how to police an unprecedented threat and students worried about fairness. The anxiety emerged after the top scorer on a national tax accountant licensing exam admitted Sunday to using a miniature camera and generative AI to cheat. The confession reversed his earlier denials, which followed public scrutiny over his unusually high marks. Amid mounting alarm over AI-assisted cheating, the government is pursuing various measures, including blocking access to public Wi-Fi at College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) sites. Teachers who spoke to The Korea Times doubted the government’s measures would do much, saying the real question for proctors is whether they can actually catch cheating even when they suspect it. results.title: Ex-justice minister Cho Kuk denied entry to Japan, Seoul expresses regret
results.content: Cho Kuk, a former justice minister and lawmaker, was denied entry to Japan Tuesday, with his party demanding an apology from Tokyo and Seoul expressing regret over the incident while requesting an explanation. Cho, who currently heads the Innovation Policy Institute — a think tank affiliated with the minor Rebuilding Korea Party — had planned a three-day visit to Japan starting Tuesday for academic exchanges, including a keynote speech at a seminar hosted by Meiji Gakuin University and meetings with Japanese experts and Korean students. Japanese authorities denied him entry at Haneda Airport in Tokyo, citing “grounds for denial of landing under Japanese law,” according to party spokesperson Im Myung-hee. “This is an unprecedented case of a public figure being denied entry to attend an academic event and deliver a keynote address at the formal invitation of a Japanese university,” Im said

results.title: Crypto winter deepens in Korea as trading slumps, growth plans stall
results.content: Korea’s cryptocurrency industry is entering a deep winter as shrinking trading volumes, deteriorating earnings and delays in launching new businesses weigh on exchanges, industry officials said Tuesday. The operators of the country’s two largest exchanges posted quarterly operating losses, while plans to open the market to corporate investors remain stalled. A series of security breaches has added to the challenge of restoring profitability and trust. Dunamu, which operates the country’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, Upbit, reported consolidated revenue of 151.7 billion won ($113 million) and an operating loss of 3.5 billion won for the third quarter, according to filings with the Financial Supervisory Service.
